# mrgsim.sa: sensitivity analysis with mrgsolve

A simple, clean workflow for sensitivity analysis with mrgsolve.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

\

``` r

library(mrgsim.sa)
```

Models in mrgsolve have “parameters” associated with them.

``` r

mod <- modlib("pk1", end = 48, delta = 0.1)

param(mod)
```

``` R
. 
.  Model parameters (N=3):
.  name value . name value
.  CL   1     | V    20   
.  KA   1     | .    .
```

Parameters are name-value pairs that are usually involved in controlling
how the system advances in time. Parameters could be clearances (`CL`),
rate constants (`k`), pharmacodynamic parameters (`EC50`) or even
covariates (`WT` … weight). mrgsim.sa does one-at-a-time sensitivity
analysis on parameters in your model.

## PK model sensitivity analysis by factor

The nominal (in model) parameter value is divided and multiplied by a
factor, generating minimum and maximum bounds for simulating a sequence
of parameter values. In this example, we vary `CL` and `V`, each one at
a time.

``` r

out <- 
  mod %>% 
  ev(amt = 100) %>% 
  select_par(CL, V) %>% 
  parseq_fct(.n = 5) %>% 
  sens_each() 

sens_plot(out, "CP")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-4-1.png)

In this sensitivity analysis, `CL` is varied at the value of `V` in the
model parameter list and `V` is varied at the value of `CL` in the model
parameter list. The black dashed line indicates the model prediction
based on `CL` and `V` both as they are in the parameter list; this is
the “reference”.

The simulated data is returned in a long format

``` r

out
```

``` R
. # A tibble: 14,520 × 7
.    case  time p_name p_value dv_name dv_value ref_value
. * <int> <dbl> <chr>    <dbl> <chr>      <dbl>     <dbl>
. 1     1     0 CL         0.5 EV             0         0
. 2     1     0 CL         0.5 EV             0       100
. 3     1     0 CL         0.5 CENT           0         0
. 4     1     0 CL         0.5 CENT           0         0
. 5     1     0 CL         0.5 CP             0         0
. # ℹ 14,515 more rows
```

The previous plot focused on relative changes in the PK profile for
“lower” and “higher” values of `CL` and `V` according to the `parseq_`
method. You can plot with a more quantitative color scale and legend
using `grid = TRUE`.

``` r

sens_plot(out, "CP", grid = TRUE)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-6-1.png)

## HIV viral dynamic model

In another example, we look at latent infected cell pool development
over ten years at different “burst” size, or the number of HIV particles
released when one cell lyses.

``` r

mod <- mread("hiv", "inst/example")

mod %>% 
  update(end = 365*10) %>%
  parseq_range(N = c(900,1500), .n = 10) %>%
  sens_each(tscale = 1/365) %>% 
  sens_plot("L", grid = TRUE)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-7-1.png)

## Sensitivity analysis on custom sequences

The model is rifampicin PBPK.

``` r

mod <- mread("inst/example/rifampicin.cpp", delta = 0.1)
```

``` R
. Building rifampicin_cpp ... done.
```

``` r

sims <- 
  mod %>% 
  ev(amt = 600) %>% 
  parseq_manual(
    SFKp = seq_fct(.$SFKp, n = 20), 
    Kp_muscle = seq_even(0.001, 0.1, n = 6)
  ) %>% sens_each() 

sens_plot(sims, "Ccentral")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-8-1.png)

# Simulate a grid

To this point, we have always used
[`sens_each()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/sens_fun.md)
so that each value for each parameter is simulated one at a time. Now,
simulate the grid or all combinations of the sensitivity parameters.

We use
[`parseq_cv()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/parseq_cv.md)
here, which generates lower and upper bounds for the range using 50%
coefficient of variation.

``` r

out <- 
  mod %>% 
  update(outvars = "Ccentral") %>%
  ev(amt = 600) %>% 
  parseq_cv(fBCLint_all_kg, .n = 5) %>% 
  parseq_cv(SFKp, Kp_muscle, .n = 3) %>% 
  sens_grid(recsort = 3) 

out
```

``` R
. # A tibble: 10,980 × 8
.    case fBCLint_all_kg  SFKp Kp_muscle  time dv_name  dv_value ref_value
. * <int>          <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> <chr>       <dbl>     <dbl>
. 1     1          0.138  3.65    0.0520   0   Ccentral     0         0   
. 2     1          0.138  3.65    0.0520   0   Ccentral     0         0   
. 3     1          0.138  3.65    0.0520   0   Ccentral     0         0   
. 4     1          0.138  3.65    0.0520   0   Ccentral     0         0   
. 5     1          0.138  3.65    0.0520   0.1 Ccentral     3.66      3.14
. # ℹ 10,975 more rows
```

``` r

sens_plot(out, "Ccentral")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-9-1.png)

The output is more complicated because all the selected parameters have
varying “sensitivity” values.

# Local sensitivity analysis

In local sensitivity analysis, we vary each sensitivity parameter a very
small amount around the parameter list (model) value and see how much
the output changes for a unit change in the parameter. The “sensitivity”
is plotted over time.

``` r

mod <- modlib("pk2", delta = 0.1, end = 48)

doses <- ev(amt = 100)

out <- lsa(mod, var = "CP", par = "CL,V2,Q,V3", events = doses)

out
```

``` R
. # A tibble: 1,928 × 5
.    time dv_name dv_value p_name     sens
.   <dbl> <chr>      <dbl> <chr>     <dbl>
. 1   0   CP         0     CL      0      
. 2   0   CP         0     CL      0      
. 3   0.1 CP         0.472 CL     -0.00254
. 4   0.2 CP         0.893 CL     -0.00514
. 5   0.3 CP         1.27  CL     -0.00782
. # ℹ 1,923 more rows
```

``` r

lsa_plot(out)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-10-1.png)

# Package index

## All functions

- [`lsa()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/lsa.md)
  [`lsa_plot()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/lsa.md)
  : Perform local sensitivity analysis
- [`mrgsim.sa`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/mrgsim.sa.md)
  : Sensitivity Analysis with 'mrgsolve'
- [`parseq_cv()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/parseq_cv.md)
  : Generate a sequence of parameters based on CV
- [`parseq_fct()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/parseq_fct.md)
  [`parseq_factor()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/parseq_fct.md)
  : Generate a sequence of parameters
- [`parseq_manual()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/parseq_manual.md)
  : Simulation helper to manually specify parameter sequences
- [`parseq_range()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/parseq_range.md)
  : Simulation helper to generate a sequence of parameters from a range
- [`parseq_reference()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/parseq_reference.md)
  : Set reference values for each parameter
- [`select_par()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/select_par.md)
  : Identify parameters in a model for sensitivity analysis
- [`select_sens()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/select_sens.md)
  : Select sensitivity runs from a sens_each object
- [`sens_each()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/sens_fun.md)
  [`sens_each_data()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/sens_fun.md)
  [`sens_grid()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/sens_fun.md)
  [`sens_grid_data()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/sens_fun.md)
  : Run an ad-hoc sensitivity analysis
- [`sens_plot()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/sens_plot.md)
  : Plot sensitivity analysis results
- [`sens_run()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/sens_run.md)
  : Run ad-hoc parameter sensitivity analyses with mrgsolve
- [`seq_cv()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/seq_cv.md)
  : Generate a sequence based on coefficient of variation
- [`seq_even()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/seq_even.md)
  : Generate evenly spaced sequence
- [`seq_fct()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/seq_fct.md)
  : Generate a sequence by fold increase and decrease from a point
- [`seq_geo()`](https://kylebaron.github.io/mrgsim.sa/reference/seq_geo.md)
  : Generate a geometric sequence of parameter values
